summary: The CAS-ANSO Scholarship (degree programme) is run by the Alliance of National and International Science Organizations for the Belt and Road Regions together with the Chinese Academy of Sciences. It supports non-Chinese master's and PhD students admitted to the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) or the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC), including studies at institutes of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Each year the degree programme supports 100 to 200 master's students and 300 PhD students. The 2026 call and its results are closed; no 2027 call was listed when checked.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must not be Chinese citizens, must be proficient in English or Chinese and must meet the international-student admission requirements of USTC or UCAS. They apply through the admission system of the university and select the CAS-ANSO Scholarship in the application. The 2026 call required master's applicants to be born on or after 1 January 1996 and PhD applicants on or after 1 January 1991.

Applicants currently studying for a master's degree in China cannot apply for the master's programme, and those currently studying for a doctorate in China cannot apply for the PhD programme; applicants who do are disqualified and their university is informed. Applying for the scholarship at both USTC and UCAS in the same cycle leads to disqualification.

Awardees must not take on other assignments during the scholarship.

ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD scholarship (a sub-category for PhD applicants): up to 40 PhD students from developing countries are selected each year by TWAS and UNESCO, with 10 scholarships prioritised for climate-related research and special, non-exclusive consideration for Least Developed Countries and women. TWAS describes the applicant as a national of a developing country in the South, holding at least a master's degree, born on or after 1 January 1991, and not currently studying for a doctorate in China. Applicants tick the box for this sub-category in the application system.

UCAS general admission rules apply on top: non-Chinese citizens in good health with a master's-equivalent degree for PhD study or a bachelor's-equivalent degree for master's study; HSK 5 with at least 180 points for Chinese-taught programmes and English proficiency for English-taught ones. USTC master's applicants need HSK 4 or above for Chinese-taught programmes or proof of English, and a clean criminal record.
age_experience_notes: Master's applicants born on or after 1 January 1996; PhD applicants born on or after 1 January 1991 (2026 call). TWAS also states an age limit of 35 for its PhD sub-category. No work experience is required in the pages read.
funding_summary: The call lists six coverage items in an image that could not be read as text. Cross-checking TWAS and UCAS pages, the benefits are: tuition waiver, a monthly stipend, health insurance, application fee waiver, one international trip to China and a one-time visa allowance. The Chinese Academy of Sciences covers all six for general awardees. For ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO awardees the Academy covers the first four and TWAS/UNESCO may cover travel and visa. PhD stipend (TWAS page): CNY 6,000 a month, or CNY 7,000 after passing the university qualification test, for up to 48 months. Master's stipend: CNY 3,000 a month for up to 36 months (carried over from stored data, from an Institute of High Energy Physics page that could not be re-read). Awardees already in China when applying get no travel subsidy. The scholarship duration is stated in the admission notice.
programmes_note: Master's and PhD degrees at USTC, UCAS or institutes of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The call states no fixed field list. UCAS admits through more than 20 faculties and more than 100 institutes across philosophy, economics, law, education, literature, history, science, engineering, agriculture, medicine, management and interdisciplinary science. USTC offers 70 master's and 82 doctoral programmes open to international students, including mathematics, physics, chemistry, materials science and engineering, electronic information, computer science and technology, geophysics and environmental science and engineering. TWAS lists agricultural, biological, medical, chemical, engineering, space and earth, mathematical, physics, and social and economic sciences for its PhD sub-category. Programme lists are on the admission sites of the two universities.
institutions_note: Study is at USTC (Hefei), UCAS (Beijing) or institutes of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, depending on where you are admitted. You apply to only one of USTC or UCAS. The same scholarship call is published by ANSO, USTC and UCAS.

summary.detail: Master's degrees at USTC or UCAS (including CAS institutes). Duration: UCAS says commonly 3 years (2 to 3 years on its older admission page); USTC says generally 2 to 3 years. Applicants born on or after 1 January 1996; not currently a master's student in China. Master's stipend of CNY 3,000 a month for up to 36 months (carried over from stored data).

benefits.conditions: UCAS charges RMB 30 per day for a shared room and RMB 60 per day for a single room to students who book campus housing; the call does not say whether CAS-ANSO awardees receive a housing benefit. USTC says on-campus housing depends on funding category and availability.

requirements.text: Online application in the USTC or UCAS admission system, selecting the CAS-ANSO Scholarship; PhD applicants tick the box for the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO sub-category. Create only one account.
Scan of the passport information page. UCAS: ordinary passport valid for at least 1 year. USTC: valid until at least September 2028 (2027 entry).
Recent two-inch bareheaded photo matching the passport photo (UCAS).
Complete CV with detailed education and research experience from university onward; an employment certificate if you are employed (UCAS).

Scans of degree certificates: bachelor's for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's for PhD applicants. Final-year applicants submit a pre-graduation certificate stating the expected date. USTC asks for notarised copies.

Complete original transcripts: undergraduate for master's applicants; master's and undergraduate for PhD applicants. Final-year applicants send transcripts to date and the complete set before registration. USTC asks for notarised copies.
English: valid IELTS or TOEFL or other proof (not required for native English speakers). Chinese-taught programmes: HSK 5 with at least 180 points at UCAS; HSK 4 or above at USTC.

UCAS: motivation letter covering purpose, academic background, reasons for applying, study plan and career goals (PhD applicants also describe research experience). USTC master's: study or research proposal of at least 1,000 words.

Two reference letters from professors or associate professors who know your academic background, on official letterhead, signed and dated; the referee cannot be the prospective UCAS supervisor. USTC asks for the referees' phone numbers and emails. Referees must submit by the deadline.
First page and abstract of up to 5 representative published papers; unpublished papers are not accepted (UCAS).
Supervisor's Acceptance Form, if a supervisor has already accepted you (UCAS).
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if you have supervisor acceptance

requirements.text: Foreigner Physical Examination Form with a sealed photo, issued within six months before submission (USTC).
Documents not in English or Chinese need a translation (UCAS: combined into one PDF with a colour scan; USTC: notarised translation).

application_steps.title: Choose USTC or UCAS and a programme
application_steps.detail: Pick one university: applying to both leads to disqualification. Check the programme list, language of instruction and the master's or PhD age limit (born on or after 1 January 1996 or 1 January 1991 in the 2026 call). Currently enrolled master's or doctoral students in China cannot apply for the same level.

application_steps.title: Prepare the university's required documents
application_steps.detail: Follow the university's call: UCAS lists passport, photo, CV, degree and transcripts, language proof, motivation letter, two reference letters and optional papers and supervisor form. USTC adds a medical form, a no-criminal-record certificate and notarised documents. Ask your referees to submit their letters in time.

application_steps.title: Apply online and select the CAS-ANSO Scholarship
application_steps.detail: Submit in the admission system of USTC or UCAS and choose the CAS-ANSO Scholarship; PhD applicants tick the box for the TWAS/UNESCO sub-category if they want to be considered. In the 2026 call applicants and referees had until 31 January 2026 (Beijing Time); the call opened on 15 October 2025. UCAS charges no application fee to scholarship applicants.

application_steps.title: University review and entrance assessment
application_steps.detail: At UCAS, admission committees review documents and pick candidates for an entrance exam, mainly an interview, with a written test at some colleges; at USTC, the college and departments review materials and invite candidates to an online assessment (interviews and possibly written exams) notified by email. USTC's 2027 timeline for its own master's call: assessment January to April 2027 and results June or July 2027.

application_steps.title: Scholarship evaluation and results
application_steps.detail: ANSO and the Chinese Academy of Sciences evaluate scholarship applications. The 2026 evaluation was completed and announced on 23 June 2026; USTC and UCAS then told applicants through their application systems or by email and issued official documents to awardees. The selection criteria are not described in the call.

application_steps.title: Visa and registration
application_steps.detail: Awardees receive an admission notice stating the scholarship duration and a visa form, apply for a study visa at a Chinese embassy or consulate and register at the time and place stated in the notice, or apply for a registration extension.

application_steps.title: Study, pass annual assessments and meet obligations
application_steps.detail: Awardees complete centralised training in Chinese language and culture, all required credits, practical research and a thesis. They pass annual assessments and qualifying tests on time, follow Chinese law and university rules, take no other assignments, and credit the scholarship in published work. Failing may end the scholarship or study, with only a certificate of attendance instead of a degree.
